title: Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part III)
gist: Gavekal argues that beyond the usual suspects behind this year's higher US bond yields (Fed balance-sheet runoff, a wider deficit from tariff refunds and the Iran war, expected Fed rate hikes, and rising JGB yields), the biggest driver may be the extraordinary fundraising boom to finance AI infrastructure, making the durability of that capex cycle the key variable for long-bond investors.

themes.theme: Conventional Drivers of Higher US Yields

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve's reduction of its long-term Treasury security holdings has pushed bond yields higher this year, prompting the Treasury to plan a twist operation to counter the effect.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Track the Treasury's twist operation as a direct, policy-driven offset to Fed balance-sheet runoff on the long end.
insights.locator: The Federal Reserve has been reducing its holdings

insights.claim: US budget deficits widened further this year as tariff refunds were distributed and the US started a new war in Iran, though only the tariff-refund driver is now starting to fade.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: With the war-related deficit driver still live, expect continued fiscal-supply pressure on Treasury issuance even as the tariff-refund effect rolls off.
insights.locator: Large US budget deficits got even larger

insights.claim: The Fed is expected to hike policy rates, a move that has helped keep inflation expectations anchored but may also be pushing up real yields.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A hiking Fed that anchors inflation expectations while lifting real yields is a bearish combination for long-duration bond prices even without an inflation scare.
insights.locator: The Fed is expected to hike policy rates

insights.claim: Japanese government bond yields have risen significantly and, combined with an attractively valued yen, may now be high enough to draw capital away from other bond markets, including US Treasuries.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Rising JGB yields plus a cheap yen is a capital-flow risk to watch for reduced Japanese demand at US Treasury auctions.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Japanese government bond yields have risen

insights.claim: The biggest driver of higher US bond yields this year may be the extraordinary amount of money being raised to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure, rather than the more commonly cited Fed and fiscal factors.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If AI fundraising is the dominant yield driver, long-bond positioning should track AI capex and credit issuance data more closely than Fed or fiscal headlines.
insights.locator: Yet the biggest driver may be something else

insights.claim: If AI infrastructure fundraising is indeed the biggest force pushing yields higher, the key question for bond investors becomes how long this capital-spending and fundraising boom will persist.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frame the long-bond call as a bet on the duration of the AI capex cycle, not just on Fed policy or fiscal trajectories.
insights.locator: If this is indeed the biggest force
